form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Cassidy (for himself, Ms. Baldwin, and Mr. Vance) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

form.official-title: To amend the Tariff Act of 1930 to require reciprocity with respect to de minimis entries of articles, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023.

section.header: Modification of treatment of de minimis entries of articles
section.text: Section 321 of Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1321) is amended—

paragraph.text: by amending subsection (a)(2)(C) to read as follows:

subparagraph.text: in any other case, such amount as the Secretary establishes under subsection (c)(1).

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.header: Reciprocity with respect to de minimis entries

clause.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023, the Secretary of the Treasury shall prescribe regulations to establish dollar amount thresholds, which may not exceed $800, for de minimis entries for purposes of subsection (a)(2)(C).
The Secretary shall establish a threshold under clause (i) for each country that takes into consideration—

subclause.text: the dollar amount threshold of that country for de minimis entries from the United States; and
any related thresholds of that country, such as a threshold relating to a value-added tax on imports.

clause.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023, the Secretary shall—

subclause.text: publish the threshold established under clause (i) in the Federal Register; and
notify the governments of foreign countries of the threshold.

clause.text: There is established within the Treasury of the United States an account to be known as the Re-shoring and Near-shoring Account (in this subparagraph referred to as the Account), consisting of such amounts as are—

subclause.text: transferred to the Account under clause (ii); and
credited to the Account under clause (iv).

clause.header: Transfer of amounts attributable to de minimis entries

subclause.text: The Secretary of the Treasury shall transfer to the Account from the general fund of the Treasury, for fiscal year 2024 and each fiscal year thereafter, an amount equivalent to the amount received into the general fund during that fiscal year that the Secretary determines is attributable to revenue received as a result of the dollar amount thresholds established under subparagraph (A).
The Secretary shall transfer amounts required by subclause (I) to be transferred to the Account not less frequently than quarterly.

clause.text: Amounts in the Account shall be available, without further appropriation, for the purposes of facilitating the movement of manufacturing from the People's Republic of China to the United States.

subclause.text: Except as provided in subclause (II), the Secretary shall invest such portion of the Account as is not required to meet current withdrawals in interest-bearing obligations of the United States or in obligations guaranteed as to both principal and interest by the United States.

subclause.header: Authorization of investment in other instruments

item.text: The Secretary may invest such portion of the Account as the Secretary anticipates will be held in the Account for not less than 2 years in equity securities or other securities through a commercial bank if the Secretary determines such investments are appropriate.
In this subclause, the terms equity security and security have the meanings given those terms in section 3(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78c(a)).

subclause.text: The interest on, and the proceeds from the sale or redemption of, any obligations held in the Account shall be credited to and form a part of the Account.

paragraph.header: Prohibition on de minimis entries from certain countries

subparagraph.text: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023, and annually thereafter, the Secretary of the Treasury shall publish a list of countries the articles of which are not eligible for entry under subsection (a)(2)(C).

clause.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023, the Secretary shall establish, and submit to Congress a report on, the conditions for including a country on the list required by subparagraph (A).
In establishing under clause (i) conditions for including a country on the list required by subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall consider the following:

subclause.text: Violations by the country of the Act entitled An Act to ensure that goods made with forced labor in the Xinjiang Autonomous Region of the People’s Republic of China do not enter the United States market, and for other purposes, approved December 23, 2021 (Public Law 117–78; 135 Stat. 1525) (commonly referred to as the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act).
Transshipment through the country of goods from countries on the list.
The exportation from the country of counterfeit goods.
Whether the government of the country is committed to the fight against trafficking in persons, illegal narcotics, and terrorism, as demonstrated by—

item.text: the government of the country not being listed under subparagraph (C) of section 110(b)(1) of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 (22 U.S.C. 7107(b)(1)) (commonly referred to as tier 3) in the most recent report on trafficking in persons required under such section (commonly referred to as the Trafficking in Persons Report); and
certification by the Department of State that the government is participating in the fight against illegal narcotics and terrorism.

subclause.text: Such other issues as the Secretary considers appropriate.

clause.text: The following countries shall be included on the list required by subparagraph (A), effective on the date of the enactment of the De Minimis Reciprocity Act of 2023:

A country specified in clause (i) may not be removed from the list required by subparagraph (A) until the Secretary certifies to Congress that the government of the country has made progress with respect to the considerations described in subparagraph (B)(ii).
The government of a country on the list required by subparagraph (A) may petition the Secretary for removal from the list.
The Secretary shall—

subclause.text: respond to a petition submitted under clause (i) not later than 90 days after receiving the petition; and
include in that response a description of any measures the government that submitted the petition is required to undertake to be removed from the list.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall consult with Congress before adding a country to or removing a country from the list required by subparagraph (A).

paragraph.header: Limitations on eligibility of carriers for importation of de minimis entries

subparagraph.text: An article is eligible for entry under subsection (a)(2)(C) only if the article is transported to the United States by a contract carrier.
A contract carrier shall provide the following data with respect to each article entering under subsection (a)(2)(C):

clause.text: The heading or subheading of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States under which the article is classifiable.
The country of origin of the article
The country of manufacture of the article (if different from the country of origin under clause (ii)).
The shipper of record.
The importer of record.
A description of the article.
The fair market value in the United States of the article.

subparagraph.text: A contract carrier transporting articles entering under subsection (a)(2)(C) shall be responsible for collecting the duties and taxes owed with respect to such articles and remitting those duties and taxes to U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
In this paragraph, the term contract carrier means a private entity that—

clause.text: is organized under the laws of the United States or any jurisdiction within the United States; and
ships small packages into the United States by air or land.

paragraph.text: In this subsection, the term de minimis entry means the entry of articles imported by one person on one day with a fair retail value that does not exceed—

subparagraph.text: in the case of articles entering the United States, the applicable threshold established under paragraph (1)(A); and
in the case of articles entering any other country, an amount determined by the government of that country to be de minimis.
